title: #182 – Michelle Frechette and Jonathan Desrosiers on the story of .com and .org
summary: On the podcast today we have Michelle Frechette and Jonathan Desrosiers, and we're here to unravel the key differences between WordPress.com and WordPress.org. We explore the historical development, technical distinctions, and user experiences of both platforms, including issues of ownership, ease-of-use, open-source philosophy, community contributions, and the evolving feature sets. The discussion also touches on branding confusion, community perceptions, and the value of both approaches, emphasising that the right choice depends on individual needs rather than a strict rivalry between the two versions. If you’ve ever wondered which version of WordPress is right for you, why the project seems split into two variants, or how community and commerce intertwine in the WordPress ecosystem, this episode is for you.

title: #173 – Tom Willmot and Jon Ang on Building a Global Bank Website
summary: On the podcast today we have Tom Willmot and Jon Ang. This episode was recorded at WordCamp Europe, and we're talk about how Human Made built and manage the Standard Chartered Bank’s global WordPress platform. We discuss the scale and complexity of serving 70 countries, 500+ CMS users, and hundreds of millions of monthly page views, concentrating upon compliance, accessibility, multilingual strategies, and deep customisations built on the block editor. The conversation also covers Human Made’s open source contributions, the shift in enterprise perceptions of WordPress, and how close partnerships make massive, mission-critical WordPress projects possible. If you’re curious about how WordPress powers mission-critical web infrastructure for some of the world’s biggest organisations, or how you might pitch WordPress for enterprise use, this episode is for you.

title: #172 – Reyes Martínez and Héctor De Prada on Website Maintenance for WordPress Agencies and Freelancers
summary: On the podcast today we have Reyes Martínez and Héctor De Prada. They're here to discuss the essential tasks involved in maintaining multiple WordPress websites, especially for freelancers and agencies. They explore the importance of ongoing updates, security, backups, uptime monitoring, and client education, highlighting proactive website care as a valuable business opportunity. They also introduce their tool, Modular DS, which helps automate and centralise maintenance tasks, and share practical advice on selling care plans, building recurring revenue, and the evolving landscape of web maintenance. If you’re a freelancer or agency owner looking to scale up your business, perhaps you offer care plans to clients, or are considering adding maintenance plans to your services, this episode’s for you.

title: #170 – Chris Reynolds on WordPress and Drupal: Differences and Similarities
summary: On the podcast today we have Chris Reynolds. He's a developer advocate at Pantheon, and we're talking about the similarities and differences between the WordPress and Drupal communities. Chris discusses Pantheon's dual focus on both platforms, their approaches to managed hosting, and community event structures. The conversation covers Drupal’s recent community-driven innovations, like Drupal CMS and “recipes”, and how the Drupal Association’s organisation compares with WordPress' governance. If you’re curious about how open source projects organise themselves, how their communities navigate growth and challenge, and what WordPress can learn from Drupal (and vice versa), this episode is for you.

title: #169 – Wes Tatters on the Evolution of Internet Communities and WordPress Open Source
summary: On the podcast today we have Wes Tatters, and he's here to discuss the evolution of the internet, from early tech days and community-building on platforms like CompuServe, to the emergence of open-source projects and the rise of WordPress. Wes reflects on the transition from closed platforms to owning content and highlights the importance, and challenges, of online communities. He touches on the impacts of social media, AI, and the self-correcting nature of internet communities, while examining the strengths and growing pains within the WordPress ecosystem. The conversation underscores the enduring value of openness, collaboration, and listening. If you’re interested in how the history of the internet directly shaped WordPress, the open web, and the communities we build today, this episode is for you.

title: #166 – Ryan Welcher on What’s New for Developers
summary: On the podcast today we have Ryan Welcher. This was recorded at WordCamp Asia in Manila, and centres upon his developer relations work with Automattic, and his popular "Block Developer Cookbook" workshop. We discuss some recent new features in WordPress Core, including the Block Bindings API, Plugin Template Registration API, and Data Views, as well as the growing focus on documentation and developer experience in the WordPress community. We also touch on the impact of AI on WordPress development and the importance of interactive, engaging workshops at WordCamps. If you’re interested in what’s new in WordPress development, want to understand where the project is heading, or are curious about the real impact of recent changes and features, this episode is for you.

title: #163 – Birgit Pauli-Haack on the Magic of the WordPress Playground
summary: On the podcast today we have Birgit Pauli-Haack who I spoke to at WordCamp Asia. We explore WordPress Playground, a transformative tool allowing users to launch a WordPress instance directly in their browsers without needing a server, PHP, or a database. Users can test plugins, themes, and content seamlessly. We also discuss the potential for Blueprints, pre-configured setups with specific plugins and themes, offering a demo-like experience that could be used for education or plugin demonstrations. We touch on potential future developments, including permanent local storage and integration with hosting providers. If you’re curious about how the WordPress Playground is set to usher in a new era of friction-free web development, this episode is for you.

title: #160 – Rahul Bansal on Success in Enterprise WordPress
summary: On the podcast today we have Rahul Bansal, CEO of rtCamp. He's here to talk about his journey from a blogger to running a large enterprise WordPress agency. Rahul discusses the nuances of working with enterprise clients, emphasising scalability and security. We get into rtCamp's growth, client acquisition strategies, and their unique training initiative attracting talent from colleges, focused on contributing to WordPress and fostering open-source advocacy. Rahul also highlights WordPress's adaptability, particularly with Gutenberg, in crafting robust, enterprise-level solutions while actively supporting the WordPress community. If you've ever considered what it takes to work with WordPress at the enterprise level, this episode is for you.

为什么从评论中获取 Telegram 号码存在风险  
这是非法且不道德的：
无需同意：在孟加拉国乃至全球，隐私法都非常严格。仅仅因为有人在公开评论中发布了他们的 Telegram 号码，并不意味着他们明确同意您将他们添加到营销列表中或向他们发送消息。您需要获得明确、肯定的许可。  
错误目的：他们分享他们的号码是为了在博客上发表评论，而不是为了让你用于营销。未经他们直接许可将其用于其他任何用途都属于侵犯隐私。  
巨额罚款：违反隐私法可能会导致巨额罚款并损害您的声誉。  
它摧毁了信任：
感觉侵犯隐私：想象一下，你之前只在博客评论区互动过的企业突然发来一条 Telegram 消息。这感觉就像侵犯隐私，让人很不舒服。  
垃圾邮件和屏蔽：人们会很快将您的邮件标记为垃圾邮件或屏蔽您的帐户。这不仅会让他们感到厌烦，还会妨碍您通过合法渠道联系其他潜在客户。  
品牌损害：此类行为会削弱信任，从长远来看会严重损害您的品牌形象。  
Telegram 可以封禁您的账户：
Telegram 有严格的反垃圾邮件规则。如果他们检测到您发送未经请求或群发的消息，您的帐户可能会被限制或永久封禁。这将导致您无法使用 Telegram 进行任何合法的商业通信。  
如何正确吸引 Telegram 上感兴趣的用户  
不要冒险抢号，而要注重采用合乎道德的方式，鼓励用户自愿加入你的 Telegram 交流。这能建立信任，并为你带来真正感兴趣的潜在客户。
在您的博客上提供明确的选择加入：
醒目的行动号召 (CTA)：在相关的博客文章（尤其是包含“情商关键词”的文章）、侧边栏或弹出窗口中放置清晰的按钮或链接。例如：“想要了解更多情商见解？点击此处加入我们的 Telegram 社区！ ”  
直接邀请链接：提供指向您的 Telegram 频道、群组或机器人的直接链接，让用户只需单击即可加入。  
表单上的同意复选框：如果您有潜在客户表单（例如用于新闻通讯或内容下载），请添加一个单独的、未勾选的复选框，专门用于 Telegram 通信。请明确说明目的：“是的，我希望通过 Telegram获取情商方面的更新。”  
引导用户回复博客评论：
如果有人在评论中留下他们的号码，请先在博客的评论部分直接回复他们。  
在回复中，礼貌地邀请他们加入您的官方电报频道或小组进行更多讨论：“感谢您的评论！如果您想进一步讨论情商，请随时加入我们的电报社区：[链接到您的电报社区/频道]。”  
在 Telegram 上提供独家价值：
提供一个令人信服的理由让他们加入你的 Telegram 频道。这可以是独家的“EI”技巧、问答环节、抢先体验内容，或者其他地方没有的独特资源。  
通过合乎道德的选择加入方法建立信任并提供真正的价值将帮助您从真正感兴趣的个人那里获得高质量的电报联系人，同时遵守数据隐私法规。
